page: Amazon Web Services m7g.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 64 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V1 CPU family running at 2.6 GHz. The processor configuration provides one thread per core, with 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It has a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps, does not include local storage, and has no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core performance and memory throughput. The server achieved a strong stress-ng multi-core score of 98,944.83 and a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 20,845.0. Memory performance is notable, with a top-tier PassMark memory score and strong read-only large block memory bandwidth of 253.89 GB/sec. Software compilation with Clang is highly efficient, scoring in the top tier at 60,170.0. However, single-core performance remains average, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,537.0.

While the server excels in multi-threaded tasks and memory-intensive operations, it exhibits limitations in specific workloads. For instance, LLM text generation using a small 135M model is weak at 73.79 tokens/sec, though prompt processing for the same model is strong at 2,890.41 tokens/sec. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage. Given its balanced resource density and high multi-core efficiency, the m7g.metal is suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and general-purpose enterprise workloads.
